messages.text: Second kiln run: 112 bowls fired, 19 rejected for crawl marks. That is 93 sellable against 140 preorder units if we open it as stock.
Then it is a preorder. I would rather take the money late than take it for a bowl that does not exist.
Preorder badge is wrong on the collection grid — issue 210. The product page is correct. Cache, not logic.
Draft one of the announcement is up. The preorder explanation is in the first paragraph, not the footer.
Jug reshot on the light ground. The old shot read grey; this one reads oatmeal, which is what it is.
Harriet has the third run booked for 27 March. She will not promise a yield and I am not going to ask her to.
Decision tomorrow: launch four pieces with the bowl on preorder. Nobody is proposing we hold the collection.
Three two-star Harbour reviews now, all describing the same crazing. I am replying on the reviews rather than by mail so the answer is public.
Replacement list is at 34 of 40. Six orders have addresses older than a year and I am mailing those to confirm before sending.
Jonas asked why his review is unbadged. He bought as a guest. That is issue 211, not a mistake on his part.
Quinn asked about the pallet on the shipping post. I said eleven orders and that we are tracing each one. No date, because we do not have one.
Alma wants a ship date for the bowl preorder. Answer after the 27th, not before.
Maren says her statement still shows two charges. The credit is a separate line, issued today. I have replied on the public thread as well.

Desmond pulled the yard log. Eight of eleven are located and were never collected. Three are still unaccounted for.
I have the eleven names. I am not sending anything until Callum can tell each of them something true.

documents.content:
# Fieldstone, 25 March

Four pieces: mug, plate, jug, serving bowl.

## The bowl

Second kiln run produced 93 sellable bowls against 140 units of demand at the last two
drops. It opens as a preorder. The announcement says so in the first paragraph.

## Open before launch

- Issue 210: preorder badge is wrong on the collection grid.
- Issue 218: preorder stock is not held against the third kiln run.

## Do not

Do not give a preorder ship date before the 27 March inspection.
documents.name: Fieldstone launch plan.md

documents.content:
# Harbour mug, first run

About forty mugs from the first Harbour run craze after repeated dishwasher cycles. The
glaze and the clay body move at different rates. It is a fit fault, not a safety fault.

## What we do

Replace every mug from that run. No return, no receipt, no proof of the fault.

## What we say

That it is ours, which run it was, and that Fieldstone uses a different glaze and a
different body and went through thirty dishwasher cycles before listing.

## Status

34 of 40 replacements sent. Six addresses need confirming first.
documents.name: Harbour mug crazing — response plan.md

documents.content:
# March duplicate charges

Two members were charged twice: club-bennett-cho and club-maren-oduya.

## Cause

The charge succeeded at the provider and the response timed out locally. The retry sent a
second charge with no idempotency key. Issue 215.

## Position

Found in reconciliation, not reported by a member. Both were told before the public post.
One credit note is issued; the second follows this week. Issue 216 means a credit note does
not yet reference the invoice it corrects, so say the invoice number in the message.
documents.name: Pantry Club duplicate charge — what we know.md

documents.content:
# Runbook: verified-buyer badges

A review is badged when its author's account id matches an order for the same product.

## Known gap

Guest checkout writes no account id, so a guest buyer is never badged. Issue 211.

## Do not

Do not badge on self-declared purchase. An unbadged real buyer is a smaller problem than
a badged stranger.

## Backfill

Rerun the matcher after any change; it is idempotent and takes about forty seconds.
documents.name: Runbook: verified-buyer badges.md

mail.body_text:
Hello,

I bought two Harbour mugs in September and both have fine cracks all through the glaze. They only ever went in the dishwasher, nothing else. I am not asking for money back, I would just like to know whether they are still safe to drink from.

Clara
mail.snippet: Fine cracks through the whole glaze after about a month of dishwasher use.
mail.subject: My Harbour mugs have cracked all over

mail.body_text:
Hello Clara,

They are safe to drink from. What you are seeing is crazing: the glaze and the clay body shrink at slightly different rates, and repeated dishwasher cycles open fine cracks in the glaze. It is a fault in our first Harbour run and it is ours.

Two replacements are going out today. Please keep the originals; there is nothing to return and no receipt needed.

Sana
mail.snippet: It is a glaze fit fault in the first run. Replacements are on the way and you keep the originals.
mail.subject: Re: My Harbour mugs have cracked all over

mail.body_text:

Hello Jonas,

Two of my four Fieldstone plates rock very slightly on a flat table. Not enough to spill anything, but I noticed. Is that expected for thrown pieces or should I send them back?

Greta

mail.body_text:
Hello Greta,

A little movement is expected: the plates are thrown and the foot is trued by hand. Our tolerance is about a millimetre. If yours rock more than that, or if it bothers you at all, say the word and we will replace them.

Otto

Kit, Mira,

mail.body_text:

My order says it shipped on 12 March and the tracking page has not changed since. I am not in a hurry but I would like to know whether it is actually moving.

Quinn

mail.body_text:
Hello Quinn,

It is not moving, and I would rather tell you that than send you back to the tracking page. Your parcel is one of eleven that were scanned onto a pallet at our warehouse on 12 March without the carrier collecting them. We are working through the yard log now.

I will write again when I can tell you where your parcel is, not before.

Otto
mail.snippet: Your parcel is one of eleven on a pallet that was scanned but not collected. We are tracing it.

mail.body_text:
Bea, Sana,

Draft attached to the response plan. Three things it has to do: name the run, explain that crazing is a glaze fit fault and not a safety problem, and say plainly that it is ours.

It must not say 'in rare cases' or 'a small number of customers may'. Forty mugs is forty mugs.

Iris
mail.snippet: It says which run, that it is a fit fault, and that it is ours. No hedging.
mail.subject: Harbour note: my draft

mail.body_text:
Iris,

Agreed on all three. One addition: say that Fieldstone uses a different glaze and a different clay body and went through thirty dishwasher cycles before we listed it. Someone will ask it in the comments within the hour and it is better said first.

Bea
mail.snippet: Agreed. One change: say the Fieldstone glaze is different, because people will ask.
mail.subject: Re: Harbour note: my draft

mail.body_text:

Your Pantry Club renewal charged twice on 1 March. A retry ran after the first charge had already succeeded. That is our bug and the credit note for 64.00 USD is issued today against invoice 2034.

mail.body_text:
Callum,

Yard log for 12 March. Pallet 4471 was scanned as outbound but the carrier collection did not happen; the driver refused the load because the manifest did not match. Eight of the eleven parcels are still in bay 3. Three are not on the pallet and I do not yet know where they are.

mail.body_text:

Callum
mail.snippet: Ship the eight today. Do not send a scan for the three until they exist.
mail.subject: Re: Pallet 4471: eight of eleven located

mail.body_text:

No ship date for the preorder until the 27 March inspection.

Mira

posts.body: Fieldstone is four pieces: a mug, a plate, a jug and a serving bowl. Everything is thrown at Harrow Works and glazed in batches of about two hundred. The bowl is the hardest of the four to get right, and the first run is short, so it opens as a preorder rather than as stock we do not have.

posts.body: About forty Harbour mugs from the first run develop fine cracks in the glaze after a few dishwasher cycles. It is a glaze fit problem, not a safety problem, and it is ours. We are writing to everyone who bought one. You do not need to send it back and you do not need a receipt.
posts.title: The Harbour mug is crazing, and we are replacing it

posts.body: Warm water, no fabric softener, and take it out of the dryer damp. Linen sheds its stiffness in about six washes and then stays that way for years.
posts.title: How to wash linen so it gets better

posts.body: Orders leave Swiftline in Columbus. A label is created when the box is packed and the first scan happens when the carrier collects, which can be a day later. If the tracking page has not moved in three days, that is a real problem and we want to hear about it.

posts.body: Every review on a product page carries a verified badge if we can match it to an order. Guest checkout does not match yet, so some genuine buyers are still unbadged. We would rather show that than badge everyone.

repositories.description: The public storefront, product pages, reviews and checkout.

issues.author: mira-halvorsen
issues.body: The product page shows the preorder state correctly. The collection grid reads a cached availability flag written before the status changed, so the Fieldstone bowl looks in stock until you open it. The drop is on 25 March.
issues.title: Preorder badge does not render on collection tiles

issues.author: anya-kowalski
issues.body: The badge is granted by matching a review author's account id to an order. A guest order has no account id, so a genuine buyer shows unbadged. Matching on the order email is the obvious fix and needs a decision about case and plus-addressing.
issues.title: Verified-buyer badge misses orders placed as a guest

issues.author: yuki-tanabe
issues.body: Most helpful first is the useful default on a product with more than ten reviews.
issues.title: Review list sorts by newest with no way to change it

issues.author: gus-ferreira
issues.body: The whole design system loads on every route. Splitting it would halve first paint on mobile.
issues.title: Product pages ship 1.4 MB of unused CSS

repositories.name: storefront

repositories.description: Orders, allocation, fulfilment webhooks and returns.

issues.author: callum-reid
issues.body: Swiftline sent eleven scans on 12 March with an empty tracking field. The service marked all eleven orders shipped and told eleven people their parcel was on its way. A scan with no tracking number is not a shipment and should be rejected.
issues.title: Shipment webhook accepts a scan with no tracking number

issues.author: otto-lindqvist
issues.body: Fixed by batching the carrier call. Closed after the wholesale return in February.
issues.title: Return label request times out above twenty items

issues.author: kit-nwosu
issues.body: Preordered bowls are not held against the second kiln run, so a walk-up order placed after the drop could take stock a preorder has already paid for.
issues.title: Backorder allocation ignores preorder quantity

repositories.name: order-service

repositories.description: Pantry Club renewals, credit notes and the monthly billing run.

issues.author: rosa-delgado
issues.body: The charge succeeds at the provider, the response times out locally, and the retry sends a second charge without an idempotency key. Two members paid twice in March. The key exists in the provider call and is not being set.
issues.title: Renewal retry can charge twice when the first attempt times out

issues.author: rosa-delgado
issues.body: A member sees a credit with no reference, which reads like an unrelated refund.
issues.title: Credit notes are not linked to the invoice they correct
